_notes: B5 — Sticker piece-out (catalog B5, plan test-plans/journey-b/b05-sticker-piece-out.md, recording docs/media/journey-b/b05-sticker-piece-out.mp4, PET-12643 automation / WEBPET-1524 manual, runner row B5).

Transport, not simulation — the sticker-to-employee lookup is device-side (the Piezas screen resolves the owner before the scan ever leaves the device), so what reaches the office is a PieceOut row that already carries its employee via EmployeeSource AlternateCode. The plan's Planner resolution (N2) proved rung 1 of the importer's FK ladder accepts that value directly — no EmployeeCodeHistory seeding, no residue.

One envelope, four records: a seeding Time In at 06:00 for 6006, two of 6006's own sticker scans at 14:27/14:28, and one scan whose employee code resolves to nothing (9999999 — the anonymous-worker rungs are off on dev), which is what makes the office fall back to the configured Undefined Employee. cardType null: the envelope mixes cardType 1 (the Time In) and 0 (the three piece-outs), so the office read queries every type and expected.cards[] states each card's own type.

codes: run-unique sticker codes in the recording's shape ('B7' + digits). A fixed sticker would blur one run's rows into the next, and a clock value would drift across retries under retry-stable References. Minted from the lineage: {code0}/{code1} are 6006's two scans, {code2} the unresolvable one.

expected.cards[3].employeeCode 'undefinedEmployee' is the reserved name for preferences.undefinedEmployee — the flow puts that id in the employee map, so the expected card and the cleanup sweep both resolve it like any other code. The device record still sends 9999999: the office is what does the falling back.

modules: Piece Payment gates piece *payment*, not piece *capture* — the importer stores NumOfPieces and resolves the employee with the module off, which is everything this spec asserts; dev reports it false only because the API reads PT_MODULES instead of TigerMaster, where it is licensed (PET-12689), so it is named, never silently skipped. Traceability - Stickers is different: without it the importer has no sticker path at all, so the traceability assertions would be vacuous — the spec asserts that one.

preconditions undefinedEmployeeSet + requireJobInEmpPieceOut: both read GET preferences once. Which exception code a job-less piece-out draws depends on the tenant — with requireJobInEmpPieceOut on it is the blocking block.fk_missing ('… is missing Job'); off, the card can only fail to pair and is flagged warn.employee_piece_job_card_not_found_plain ('No corresponding Job-Card was found for Piece-Out record.'). WEBPET-2657 retired the interim 'JobCounter is required…' text. The test expects exactly one of the two, never either.

expected.grid: the Transfer screen is the proof, read after Analyze. rowStatus is the badge each card reads — the two sticker cards Blocking when requireJobInEmpPieceOut is on, Warning when off (missingJobRequired / missingJobOptional); the card that fell to the Undefined Employee is Blocking either way, because the fallback owner is itself unusable and that supersedes the missing job. issueGroups are leading-text patterns of the Issues-panel groups (each must affect at least one record). They were not measured live when written (no untransferred cards on the measuring tenant): the first run on a fixture day calibrates them, and a miss names every group the panel showed.

dayOffset -7 keeps 6006's employee-day away from B4 (-8) and B6 (-6) under workers=2. cleanup: the timeCards step sweeps 6006's and the Undefined Employee's fixture day (both card types) before the import and deletes every imported card after the test — including the Undefined-Employee card; the flow passes sweep:false so exactly one cleanup path is live.
